summary: DAT-B: coverage + injectivity. Injectivity LANDED (worksheet 0.4/2, consumed not proved).

B-6 IS CLOSED 2026-07-29 (run 0072 r5, lane ajcr-charts, commit b4d608389). This row said B-6
"still waits on divRep through C9b, whose own gate is now the single clause IsChartUniv". Both
halves of that sentence were wrong. B-6 waits on NOTHING divRep-side, and C9b's gate is not a
single clause (see the c9b row's retraction).

WHAT B-6 ACTUALLY WAS: three files carry
[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] as a variable --
JacobianDataCharts.lean:117, JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183, JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131 --
and NOTHING anywhere produced one. That gap is now filled, certificate-free and divRep-free,
in Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean (sorry-free, rooted, axiom-clean against firing
controls):

 * ChartsCoverLocally -- the coverage hypothesis, stated as "for every test T and every
   degree-zero class s on it, the SUPREMUM of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering
   sieve". Deliberately per-chart rather than on the coproduct, so a producer discharges it by
   exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one index per point of T and never reasons about a
   coproduct of yoneda presheaves. This is B-5 verbatim.
 * isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc -- B-6. The image sieve of Sigma.desc f contains each f i's
   (transport a witness along Sigma.iota, then Sigma.iota_desc), hence their supremum, and a
   sieve containing a covering sieve is covering.

SO B-6 IS NOT A GEOMETRIC OBLIGATION ON TOP OF B-5: it is B-5 phrased against mathlib's sieve
interface plus that bookkeeping. And what the proof shows to be ABSENT is what lanes worried
about -- NO cross-chart compatibility and NO injectivity are needed, because Sigma.desc imposes
no coherence across indices. That is the Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree observation about hf, holding
again for coverage: the CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEITY recorded below is not an obstruction to
B-6 either.

Hypothesis checked SATISFIABLE, not assumed: chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective derives it
from a single chart surjective on every test. Degenerate, and not the geometry -- but it rules
out an unsatisfiable Prop making the reduction vacuous.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S ACCOUNTING: what stands between the tree and the local-surjectivity
instance is now exactly B-5, i.e. ChartsCoverLocally. Everything downstream of B-5 on the
coverage side is discharged. The B-5 residue itself is unchanged and is stated below.

Coverage (COV-1 = B-5) is ASSEMBLED over a general test and owes ONE residue -- but the residue is
NOT the one this row claimed yesterday.

B-4 OPENNESS: CLOSED 2026-07-29 (run 0072 s0010, commit 2b6228f6a). CHART-U(b) at a general test is
now UNCONDITIONAL -- isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal' (Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean),
IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant discharged. See the c9-chartlocus.chart-u row for the instance-side
pricing lesson that came out of it.

B-5 STEP 3 -- RETRACTED AND RESTATED 2026-07-29 (I-0660; commits e3593861a + 05cad5d80).
This row said step 3 was "STILL the residue, but now DERIVED not chosen ... so what remains is
INSTANTIATING DAT-0a at the base-changed curve C_L". That is FALSE. A reviewer measured it and
three machine-checked statements now replace it (Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean):

 * ledger_forces_b_eq_n -- at a chart index legal at parameter n (the constraint
   deg_k Z = m*d1 - n that chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup requires) the hdeg hypothesis of
   mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound DETERMINES the threshold: b = n. It was never an input DAT-0a
   could supply.
 * hb_forces_h0_eq_one -- at n = g the resulting hb forces EVERY degree-g divisor to have h0 = 1
   (rank anchor + chi-ledger). That is FALSE on a curve with a moving degree-g family, so there is
   no route through b = g at all. This SHARPENS the reviewer, who priced it as "stronger than any
   threshold result in the tree" -- it is stronger than what is true. DAT-0a's own bound is
   n1*deg F + g with 0 < deg F, hence strictly above g for n1 >= 1.
 * index_of_threshold -- what survives, and it corrects the reviewer's conclusion: hdeg IS
   satisfiable for every b >= 0, at chart parameter n := b.toNat, because n is FREE across the
   whole chart layer (divFunctor, chartValue, chartValueTrans, abelSigmaChart are all stated at
   arbitrary n; n = g is where the DIVISOR REPRESENTABILITY lane instantiates, not something the
   coverage theorem knows). So coverage-at-an-index is not blocked.

THE RESIDUE, therefore, is neither prior reading: it is RECONCILE THE CHART PARAMETER WITH THE
THRESHOLD -- carry the slack in Z at parameter g, the g + e shape classDeg_presenting_twist_eq_add
already has, whose legality (worksheet 1.1 demands 0 <= Sigma AND deg = m*d1 - g) is the open
question. That is also not the reviewer's proposed repair verbatim: they proposed restating with
slack and themselves noted it collides with that legality.

(Picard/DegreeZeroBaseField.lean, unconditional in L/K); step 6 RETRACTED as unnecessary since
IsSplitWitness asks for h1 = 0 and for neither effectivity nor degree g
(Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean). The reviewer independently re-verified both of those and
neither is disturbed.

WHERE THE DISCARDED PROPERTIES DO MATTER: effectivity and h0 = 1 are needed by DAT-C's canonical
section and GAP-2 uniqueness, i.e. by INJECTIVITY, not by coverage.

B-6 (the IsLocallySurjective instance + DAT-glue handoff) -- SUPERSEDED, see the B-6 IS CLOSED
section at the top of this row. What stood here read "still waits on divRep through C9b, whose
own gate is now the single clause IsChartUniv"; both clauses are false as of 2026-07-29. B-6
needed nothing divRep-side (isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc, commit b4d608389) and C9b's gate was
never a single clause (see the c9b row).

CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS, which reshapes the residue above once more -- and this correction
applies to my own restatement as much as to the reviewer's.

Both readings above reason about "the" chart parameter as if the atlas had one. It does not.
pic0RepresentableByOfCharts takes a family over an ARBITRARY index type with a PER-INDEX
certificate and NO coherence condition across indices, so nothing ties the chart parameters of
different charts together. mixedParamChart builds such a family from nn : iota -> N with a
per-index representation of divFunctor C pi (nn i) and a per-index index legal AT THAT index's own
parameter; mixedParamRepresentableBy feeds it to the DAT-glue seam verbatim.

CONSEQUENCE: b = n is a PER-CHART calibration. A point whose splitting field has threshold b_L can
be covered by the chart of parameter b_L.toNat and a different point by a different chart -- so the
I-0204 non-uniformity of m is NOT an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument FOR an atlas
indexed by the threshold.

WHAT IS STILL MISSING, and it is now a question for ajcr-divrep rather than for this lane:
mixedParamChart takes rep i as a HYPOTHESIS, one representation per parameter, and the divRep
endpoint (divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause, DivRepAffPullClause.lean:475) is at g. So the

   threshold, and the b = n forcing is harmless;
 - if it is g-only: the slack must go into Z at parameter g, and the legality question above (0 <=
   Sigma AND deg = m*d1 - g) is the real residue.

Not weakened by this: IsChartUniv (CERT-Sigma-gated) and local surjectivity / B-6, which is what
would actually consume the freedom.
